dedupe_keys.name: twinyields digital twin of a crop farm at luke jokioinen 2022 2023

description: TwinYields was a project of the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) to build a prototype digital twin of a crop farm and use it to model and monitor the smart farming field infrastructure at Luke's Jokioinen research site in real time. The twin couples the open-source APSIM agricultural systems simulator with standard farm management information system plans, sensor data obtained through APIs, soil scans and publicly available remote sensing data, which Luke notes had not previously been combined with APSIM's simulation engine. It was run by Luke, led by Victor Bloch and Matti Pastell, and funded by Luke from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2023. The study covers fields at one research farm in Finland, with a longer-term aim of simulating all Luke research farms and commercial farms, including livestock. The software was developed openly, with documentation on the project website, free to read. Caveats: the project page describes aims, not results, and it does not state a licence or the status of the software after 2023. For simulation it is a worked example of linking a process-based crop model to live field data, the core of digital twins that assess management choices and climate change effects on yields. It is related to the APSIM record in this catalogue, the simulation engine it builds on.
